title: Rollout controller: add SLO evaluator hook (pause/rollback integration point)
creator: Jada Williams
body:
## Context
We need a stable integration point in the rollout controller state machine to evaluate rollout-scoped SLO signals (latency/error-rate/etc) and decide whether to proceed, pause, or rollback. This ticket is specifically for the controller-side hook + feature-flag strategy + acceptance tests. SLO querying + debounce/policy comes from follow-on tickets (policy engine + monitor adapter).

This is the first step toward the broader project: auto-rollback/pause on SLO breach during canary/A-B/staged model deployments.

## Goal
Add an SLO evaluator hook that runs during rollout progression and produces a structured decision result that can be acted on by the controller (initially: PAUSE only), with strict safeguards:
- no behavior change unless explicitly enabled
- no blocking rollouts when monitor data is missing/stale (fail-open by default, with explicit outcome recorded)
- idempotent behavior under retries / controller restarts

## Proposed hook location(s)
Hook should execute at a well-defined point in the controller loop:
- before advancing traffic step (e.g., 10% -> 25%)
- before promotion to next stage/model version
- optionally after step completion to catch immediate regressions (post-step check), but MVP can be pre-advance only

Decision should be evaluated against the *current rollout scope*:
- service/route
- model version(s) involved in step
- region
- customer tier

## Feature flag strategy
1) Controller-level flag gate (hard off by default)
- Flag name: rollouts.sloEvaluationHook (internal)
- Default: OFF in all envs
- Enabled first in dev/staging only

2) Per-rollout policy gate (soft enable)
- Even if controller flag is ON, only run evaluator when the rollout policy config indicates SLO-driven actions are configured.
- This prevents accidental evaluation for legacy policies.

3) Action gating
- MVP: allow outcome == PAUSE only (no automated rollback execution yet)
- Later: allow ROLLBACK once rollback executor + audit trail + policy safe-bounds ship

## Implementation notes
- Define an interface in the rollout controller package:
  - Evaluate(ctx, rolloutID, scope, step) -> Decision
- Decision is a small object with fields (serialized into audit logs later):
  - outcome: PROCEED | PAUSE | ROLLBACK | SUPPRESSED | INSUFFICIENT_DATA | MONITOR_STALE
  - reason_code (string enum)
  - monitor_refs (opaque ids/strings, can be empty)
  - evaluated_at (timestamp)
  - details (single string summary; keep it short to avoid high-cardinality)
- For this ticket, the evaluator implementation can be a stub / adapter facade that returns PROCEED unless a test override is active.
- Ensure controller does not spam evaluation on tight loops:
  - only evaluate once per step transition attempt (or on a periodic cadence with a minimum interval)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Hook executes at the agreed state-machine point and is covered by unit tests.
- [x] When feature flag is OFF: no calls to evaluator and no behavior changes.
- [x] When feature flag is ON but policy is missing/disabled: evaluator is not called.
- [x] When evaluator returns PAUSE: rollout transitions to PAUSED state with a clear internal reason (string) and is resumable.
- [x] Hook behavior is idempotent (retries do not double-apply pause / duplicate step state).
- [x] Basic integration test uses a fake evaluator to force PAUSE and verifies state + emitted controller log line (audit event comes later).

## Test plan
Unit tests (controller package):
- test_flag_off_does_not_invoke_evaluator
- test_policy_missing_does_not_invoke_evaluator
- test_evaluator_pause_sets_state_and_stops_advancement
- test_evaluator_proceed_allows_step_advance
- test_idempotent_pause_on_retry

Staging smoke (manual):
- Enable flag in staging
- Run a synthetic rollout with evaluator stub set to PROCEED -> ensure no behavior change
- Force evaluator stub to PAUSE at step boundary -> ensure controller pauses and can be resumed

## Rollout / enablement
- Land behind rollouts.sloEvaluationHook flag
- Enable in staging for E2E tests only (see ENG-4844)
- Do not enable in prod until monitor adapter + policy schema + audit trail are ready

## Links
- Confluence PRD: auto-rollback on SLO breach integration (Console & Rollouts)
- Design spec: rollout-controller SLO monitoring integration
- Related PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-28411-rollout-controller-hook-slo-evaluator.json
- Follow-on: ENG-4822 (policy schema), ENG-4826 (monitor adapter), ENG-4837 (metrics)

## Open questions
- Do we need a post-step evaluation hook in MVP, or can we rely on pre-advance checks + alerting? (Recommendation: keep MVP pre-advance only; add post-step once debounce logic is in place.)
- Fail-open vs fail-closed when monitors are stale/missing. MVP should fail-open and record outcome; policy can add stricter behavior later.
activity_log: 2026-02-10 (Jada Williams): Created ticket after spike discussion; agreed to start with controller hook gated behind a flag; MVP action is PAUSE only.
2026-02-12 (Jordan Lee): Requested that the hook return a structured outcome enum (not boolean) so policy engine + audit trail can consume consistent reason codes later.

2026-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): Confirmed fail-open preference for missing/stale monitor data in MVP; avoid blocking rollouts due to telemetry lag. Add explicit outcome code for MONITOR_STALE/INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
2026-02-18 (Jada Williams): Implemented hook + basic fake evaluator in tests; added per-rollout policy gate to avoid calling evaluator for legacy rollouts.
2026-02-20 (Chloe Martin): Review feedback: ensure pause is resumable and does not corrupt step state; add idempotency test for pause on controller retry.
2026-02-24 (Jada Williams): Merged via PR-28411. Flag remains OFF by default; staging enablement only for E2E coverage.
